evidence.note: Repeated numbered plans exist but describe reading order of the reference (migrations, views, middleware), not milestone sequencing of the port with done-checks.

Module-level decomposition (Cargo.toml → db → models → handlers → middleware → jobs → templates) is stated and all modules are written before any compile — a monolithic push rather than a runnable skeleton first.
Long compile-error and file-loss spiral; no /_health-first milestone, no parity/done-checks per subsystem, and hard pieces (job queue, FTS5, feeds) never deliberately de-risked.

Only at the very end, as a rescue, does the agent adopt a skeleton-first idea ('minimal app that compiles... pass the basic health check'), showing the health-first milestone concept arrived too late to structure the work.

reasoning: The agent produced an ordered breakdown into subsystems/modules with rough priorities, which exceeds a mere vague feature list (anchor 3), but it lacked sequencing rationale and per-milestone completion criteria and — decisively — never stood up a working skeleton before feature work, instead building everything monolithically and only discovering the health-first idea at step 117 as damage control. This falls short of the anchor-5 requirement of 'a working skeleton before feature work,' placing it at a 4 between the vague-list (3) and sensible-ordered-with-skeleton (5) anchors.
